Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Dedicated Capacity Sizing — Next steps

Thanks again for the call today, Elena — good to meet the FinTechCo team. This thread will capture the immediate next steps for sizing Dedicated capacity and validating we can meet the performance SLOs you outlined. Summary from our side:

- Primary SLOs discussed: p95 latency <= 120 ms for short responses (<= 40 tokens); p99 latency <= 250 ms.
- Streaming requirement: yes — response tokens must be delivered as they are generated (server-side streaming) with start-of-stream latency target <= 150 ms.
- Concurrency & throughput: baseline concurrency target 75 concurrent streams, peak concurrency up to 250. Expected baseline sustained QPS ~50 req/s, peak burst to ~350 req/s for 30-60s windows.
- Model(s): you said preference for an open 13B with quantization; possible test against a 70B 4-bit variant later.
- Success criteria for POC: meet p95/p99 at baseline concurrency and demonstrate graceful degradation (fallback to lower-cost variant) at peaks.

Action items I have captured: 
1) FinTechCo: share representative prompt set + average/median/95th token lengths for generation, and confirm if sampling will be deterministic or top-k/top-p.
2) Infra: confirm if TLS termination is on your side (we need perf numbers with and without TLS offload).
3) Redwood: Aditya will run a sizing validation across A100/H100/L4 profiles and propose a reserved throughput (vCPU/GPU pool sizing) workbook attached.

I attached our latest sizing workbook (redwood-dedicated-sizing-v2.xlsx) and a short doc with p99 targeting assumptions (p99-latency-reqs.pdf). Please review and let us know if the baseline numbers above need adjustment. Once we have the prompt set + token distributions we can schedule a 2-day validation window next week.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — copying the proposed technical plan below and a few clarifying questions so we can prepare the bench tests. High level plan: run parallel benchmarks on 3 GPU profiles (A100 40GB, H100 80GB, L4 48GB) with your representative prompt set and the following axes:
- Concurrency sweep: 1 -> 300 concurrent streams
- Throughput sweep: sustained QPS at 10/50/150 and burst profiles up to 350 QPS
- Streaming behavior: measure first-token latency, token delta (per-token latency), and end-to-end generation time
- Quantization & KV cache: test FP16, 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants; measure memory/KV cache hit behavior for prompt prefixes

Clarifying questions for FinTechCo: 
- Typical request size (input tokens) and average total response tokens? (Marissa requested this but I want numbers in this thread)
- Are you using streaming for every call or only long-form responses?
- Any hard CPU constraints on the client side (we can run with TLS offload to a LB if you prefer)

Deliverables after the 2-day run: detailed perf matrix (CSV), recommended reserved throughput and GPU counts for a committed tier, and a runbook for graceful degradation (auto-fallback targets and routing policies).

I’ll start the test harness and share results in a shared folder; please drop the prompt set into the folder linked by Marissa or reply here.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer — Performance
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Vivek / Aditya — thanks for the clear summary and plan. Quick answers from our side: 
- Typical request: 45 input tokens, median response ~48 tokens, 95th percentile response length ~210 tokens.
- Streaming: yes for any response >40 tokens (we need partial tokens delivered to the browser as they generate).
- Determinism: sampling will be stochastic (top-p ~0.92); we can provide a deterministic test vector if needed for debugging but production will be stochastic.
- TLS termination: handled by our LB (we will provide a test endpoint with TLS offload disabled if you need raw perf numbers).

We dropped a zipped sample prompt set and our procurement questionnaire in the shared folder (I’ll also attach the PPT here). We can commit to providing the prompts by EOD Monday. Please go ahead and book the 2-day validation window on your side (we prefer 4/7–4/8). Invite our infra alias and myself.

On procurement: our security team will request SOC 2 Type II evidence and an export controls attestation before contract signature. If you can share SOC 2 artifacts or a portal link early, that will help speed procurement.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
